result.keyword: Which luxury real estate agencies or buyers advocates in Australia offer the best buyers advocacy and acquisition advisory for prestige homes?
result.markdown:
For prestige homes in Australia, I would distinguish between **independent buyers’ advocates who represent only the buyer, luxury acquisition advisers who source and negotiate discreetly off-market, and prestige real estate agencies that offer buyer-side services or access to high-end property networks.** They can all be valuable, but they don't offer the same level of independence or depth of acquisition advice.

For a multimillion-dollar home, the best adviser should do more than find attractive listings. They should identify opportunities before they reach the market, assess fair value, investigate comparable sales and property risks, negotiate strategically, and coordinate due diligence through to settlement.

## My shortlist of Australian prestige property advisers

The following are the firms I would investigate first, depending on the city, type of property and level of acquisition support required. This is a qualitative shortlist, not a verified ranking of transaction success or client satisfaction.

![Primrose Property Consultants | Advocates For Luxury Homes Melbourne](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/HBWUMTn5RGWQfrreXmIKF1V2-psuonjrwVbpkX4lslf_-Ac88iK1abV2ilZQkbA1bHHUjwjQOGhBk8ExhuHTqwADtFkgtxIHEFzxNeIO5OXSL7XWJrml0c9SKsiZ2Pet22_OvrduzCv3KBwJqJRyXCWDH_-Qw_5bMd-UM8jNluSyeDpOCvo4EO6IN6n_iT39?purpose=fullsize)

## 1\. Propertybuyer

(Best national starting point)

Propertybuyer has a broad buyer-advocacy operation, with dedicated advisers across prestige markets including Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast. Its published offering emphasises exclusive buyer representation, market knowledge and access to high-end opportunities. **Best for\:** A substantial acquisition brief, an interstate or overseas buyer, or someone who wants one firm to coordinate the search across more than one city.

Website: [prestigepropertybuyer.com.au](https://prestigepropertybuyer.com.au/)

## How I would choose between them

| Your priority | First firms I'd interview |
|--------|--------|
| National reach or interstate relocation | Propertybuyer |
| Independent Melbourne prestige acquisition | Buyer's Advocate |
| Toorak, Armadale, Malvern, Hawthorn or Kew | Primrose |
| Melbourne premium-market research and sourcing | Infolio |
| Broader agency network and a structured search | Cohen Handler |
| Valuation-oriented negotiation and advisory | Greville Pabst Property Advisory |


These are best-fit matches based on their published services and market focus, not proof that one firm consistently achieves better purchase prices than another.

## Prestige real estate agencies versus independent buyers' advocates

If you are purchasing a home worth, say, \$5 million to \$20 million or more, I would consider the following distinction particularly important.

**Independent buyers' advocates**

They are engaged to represent your interests, source properties, advise on value and negotiate. This is generally my preferred model for a buyer who wants confidential, unconflicted acquisition advice. The Real Estate Buyers Agents Association of Australia (REBAA) outlines independence, licensing and conflict-of-interest standards for its members. [rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/buyers-agents/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/REBAA-Code-of-Conduct-2024-Edition-v5.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

**Prestige sales agencies**

Firms such as Ray White and Kollosche can be useful sources of market intelligence, listing access and introductions to premium properties. Kollosche is especially relevant to the Gold Coast prestige market. [www.couriermail.com.au](https://www.couriermail.com.au/property/gold-coast-luxury-property-market-defies-national-downturn-as-wealthy-interstate-buyers-invest/news-story/7e04ade24dcc8907cb6a9ff61953cbfb?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.couriermail.com.au](https://www.couriermail.com.au/real-estate/queensland/gold-coast/economist-reveals-major-shift-in-gold-coast-property-market/news-story/4995cd6b00c7465cf45b7259ccc6850d?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

However, a selling agent's primary responsibility is to the vendor. I would use these agencies as sources of opportunities rather than assume their advice is equivalent to independent buyer representation.

## What to demand from an acquisition adviser

For a prestige purchase, I would insist on six things before signing an engagement agreement\:

1. **Relevant transactions\:** Three recent purchases comparable in price, suburb and property type, with client references where possible.
2. **Genuine off-market access\:** Evidence of relevant opportunities sourced before public listing, not just a large contact database.
3. **Independent valuation discipline\:** Comparable sales, a defensible price range, an assessment of the property's weaknesses and a clear walk-away price.
4. **Confidentiality\:** A documented process for protecting your identity, budget and negotiating position.
5. **Full due diligence\:** Coordination with your conveyancer or solicitor, building and pest inspectors, and relevant planning or specialist advisers.
6. **Transparent fees and conflicts\:** Written disclosure of commissions, referral payments, developer relationships and any other financial interests.

REBAA publishes useful guidance on choosing an advocate and typical fee structures. Its published industry guidance puts full-service fees commonly around 2–3% of the purchase price plus GST, although fixed-fee arrangements and more limited negotiation-only services are also available. Obtain individual quotes rather than treating this as a universal tariff. [rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/buyers-agents/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/faqs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

search_results.title: Longhurst Property launches in Townsville with 50 deals in year one
search_results.description: Longhurst Property, founded by Nathan Longhurst, officially launched as an independent real estate agency in January 2026 after previously operating under the Professionals franchise. Leveraging Mr. Longhurst's international sales experience, the agency quickly gained momentum, completing approximately 50 property transactions within its first year. Specializing in various residential properties, the firm expanded from zero to four staff members. The current Townsville real estate market has shifted due to government tax changes, causing a reduction in investor activity and a rise in owner-occupier buyers. This led to a growing inventory of available homes, increasing from 250-300 to 600-700 properties. Longhurst highlighted the importance of property pricing, presentation, and marketing, emphasizing that the right strategy can turn it into a sellers' market. The agency secured a prominent office location at 219 Charters Towers Rd, Mysterton—a former book shop and Asian supermarket—which was purchased for $560,000 and renovated. The property offers high visibility and includes four onsite parking spaces, supporting the firm’s operational needs.

search_results.title: Gold Coast luxury property defies downturn as Sydney buyers move in
search_results.description: Despite a nationwide property downturn that has reverted prices and sales to 2023 levels, the Gold Coast luxury real estate market remains resilient. This strength is attributed to a limited housing supply, robust internal migration, and affluent buyers—particularly from Sydney—seeking better value. Michael Kollosche, managing director of Kollosche, highlights how high-end Gold Coast apartments, priced between $25,000 and $35,000 per square metre, offer better value compared to Sydney's $120,000 per square metre rates. Notable recent sales include an $11.5 million penthouse purchase by a European investor. According to Colliers, Gold Coast property prices have surged 84% since 2021, surpassing Brisbane and Greater Brisbane. Analyst Michael Matusik notes a shift from investment properties to owner-occupied beachfront homes, as the city attracts wealthy buyers post-pandemic. Downsizing among affluent homeowners along Hedges Avenue is driving demand for luxurious, smaller residences in the same prime locations. This demographic shift is shaping a robust, high-end market insulated from broader sectoral declines.

search_results.title: Ray White TMG Luxury launches amid Gold Coast market downturn
search_results.description: Ray White TMG Luxury has launched amid a downturn in the Gold Coast property market, marked by four interest rate hikes, Middle East conflict, and changes to federal property tax policies. Ray White chief economist Nerida Conisbee remarked on the market’s uncertainty, though noting it is currently easier to transact. The launch featured a premium Broadbeach Waters property at 29 Namatjira Court with 95m of river frontage, 533 sq m of luxury living space, and high-end amenities such as a cocktail lounge and riverside pool. Despite a 3% decline in overall Gold Coast property values over the past year, the luxury segment in Broadbeach Waters remains resilient, mirroring stabilizing trends in Sydney’s Eastern suburbs and Melbourne’s South Yarra and Toorak. The event also marked the official unveiling of Ray White TMG Luxury, a new prestige-focused division led by CEO Matt Micallef. Micallef emphasized the division’s goal to provide a specialist approach for high-end buyers and sellers, asserting the Gold Coast's legitimacy as a top-tier luxury market. The luxury brand aims to respond to growing demand with dedicated, high-caliber service.

search_results.title: Aria's Sanctuary Residences: $519m sold before public launch
search_results.description: Aria Property Group has reported a record-breaking pre-launch success for its Sanctuary Residences project in South Brisbane, achieving $519 million in apartment sales, making it Queensland’s largest apartment launch to date. Remarkably, sales were made without any public advertising, focusing on high-end three and four-bedroom apartments priced from $2.72 million and $4.01 million. Of the 231 apartments available in the first tower, only 86 remain unsold. Designed for buyers seeking spacious, luxurious homes without downsizing, the project has attracted strong interest. The development at 164-190 Melbourne Street includes restoration of two heritage buildings and features expansive amenities such as a wellness club, rooftop bar, and 2.9-meter ceilings. It is part of a larger master-planned precinct with public parks, laneways, and retail spaces. The first tower is set to complete by mid-to-late 2029, aligning with Brisbane's preparation for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. This overwhelming response reflects growing demand for high-quality apartment living in Brisbane. The remaining units will be publicly released on October 19, with potential price increases expected.

search_results.title: Inside Katanga: Hamilton's grand 1884 riverfront estate for sale
search_results.description: Katanga, a prestigious 1884 riverfront estate in Hamilton, Brisbane, is now on the market after an extensive transformation blending historical charm with modern luxury. Located at 25 Langside Road on a 1113 m² plot, the home has been thoughtfully redesigned by Twohill & James, maintaining its original heritage while introducing contemporary, lift-connected living across three levels. Current owners Sam and Brad Hopper, who previously owned a prominent Sunshine Beach property, sought to honor the home's history through elegant updates, including Calacatta Viola marble and travertine finishes. The residence features five ensuite bedrooms, including a luxurious parents' retreat, a self-contained guest wing, and numerous leisure amenities such as a gym, sauna, cinema, alfresco terrace, wet-edge pool, and heated spa. The impressive kitchen and entertaining areas integrate seamlessly with modern family functionality, while features such as a 10-car garage, dual EV chargers, and private office further enhance its appeal. With its sweeping river views and seamless blend of old and new, Katanga is a rare Brisbane gem now ready for new owners.

search_results.title: Villa Alcyone: Award-winning Elanora mansion eyes suburb record
search_results.description: Villa Alcyone, a Mediterranean-style mansion situated on a steep 890 sqm block at 6 Bicton Ct in Elanora, has entered the market with expectations to surpass the suburb's sales record by millions. Designed by Jayson Pate and built by Resolve Constructions, the award-winning home reflects a growing trend of luxury builders tackling challenging vertical sites. The property garnered multiple accolades at the 2026 HIA Gold Coast and Northern Rivers Awards and a Master Builders Queensland award. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom home spans 579 sqm and features high-end finishes such as Italian marble, dramatic archways, and a Sukabumi stone pool, all inspired by European influences during the owners' travels. Interior design was led by co-owner Helen Foukkare. Positioned to maximize ocean views and offering access to popular nearby beaches like Currumbin and Palm Beach, the mansion is drawing interest from high-end buyers typically focused on more traditionally prestigious areas. Although quarterly data shows a slight dip in Elanora home prices, the suburb's annual values rose 14.7 percent, reflecting its evolving luxury market appeal. The Foukkares are already planning another unique luxury build in the Gold Coast region.

search_results.title: Graya breaks ground on Brisbane's most expensive house in New Farm
search_results.description: Celebrity developers Graya have commenced construction on a lavish mansion dubbed “Ivory,” on an exclusive riverfront block in New Farm, Brisbane, purchased by Chemist Warehouse boss Jeff Wasley and his wife Tanya for a record-breaking $25 million in 2025. Designed and built by Graya over 11 months, the home is expected to be worth between $40-$50 million upon completion. The 688 sqm site was previously owned by Graya co-founder Rob Gray and originally intended as his personal residence before it was sold for a $16.5 million profit. Ivory features a five-storey design including high-end amenities such as a luxury car showroom with river views, resort-style pools, rooftop entertainment areas, a wellness center, state-of-the-art golf simulator, and a master suite with 10-meter wardrobes. The house boasts a sleek, neutral finish with white, curved terraces and mushroom-style pillars. Located between New Farm Park and the Story Bridge, the property offers panoramic views of Brisbane’s skyline. This milestone build reflects Graya’s continued influence in Brisbane's luxury real estate market. The Wasleys had previously acquired another Graya-built home in Hamilton for $12.5 million.

search_results.title: Brisbane, Gold Coast apartment crisis: $5.4bn backlog revealed
search_results.description: A construction crisis has emerged in Brisbane and the Gold Coast, with 112 apartment projects, totaling 10,286 dwellings and valued at $5.4 billion, currently deferred or indefinitely suspended due to soaring construction costs and labor shortages. Brisbane alone accounts for 6,711 apartments across 71 projects ($2.5bn), while the Gold Coast records 3,575 apartments in 41 projects ($2.9bn). PRD chief economist Dr. Diaswati Mardiasmo warns that many approved developments may never be built as construction costs have more than doubled since 2020, and builders are fully booked for years. Major projects like Breakfast Creek Quarter and Urban Forest are on hold, highlighting broader challenges in housing supply. Although some developers affirm their commitment to future delivery, uncertainty prevails. The Property Council of Australia urges policy changes to unlock supply pipelines, warning that approvals alone are insufficient. Meanwhile, risks of buyer settlement defaults loom, with some developers seeking alternative selling strategies. Despite signs of partial recovery in project values, Queensland remains structurally undersupplied, affecting affordability for first-home buyers and renters, and posing long-term challenges for housing availability.

search_results.title: Ferrari fan's $4.3m Doncaster East buy after 5hrs of inspections
search_results.description: A luxury home in Doncaster East, Melbourne, known as Saxonwood, sold for $4.3 million—marking the suburb’s highest sale since 2024. The sale followed an unusual private-inspection strategy, where qualified buyers received 45-minute one-on-one appointments. The eventual buyer, a Ferrari enthusiast and seasoned tarmac rally participant, spent over five hours inspecting the home across multiple visits. Though the property included car-centric features such as a four-car automotive gallery and over 2.5 tonnes of calacatta marble in the kitchen, it was its location—opposite Zerbes Reserve with unobstructed park views through floor-to-ceiling windows—that ultimately secured the sale. The home garnered national and international interest and went under contract after 24 days, with negotiations concluding over 13 days. The campaign included an exclusive launch event featuring $15 million worth of luxury cars and Italian food and wine, emphasizing the property's automotive and European design themes. The buyer, also planning to visit Ferrari’s factory in Italy for a custom car and to add a swimming pool post-settlement, was swayed by the unique outlook from the main living area, stating the experience of the park view sealed the decision to purchase. Agent Daniel D’Assisi now plans to replicate this marketing strategy for other high-end homes.

For prestige homes in Australia, I would distinguish between **independent buyers’ advocates who represent only the buyer, luxury acquisition advisers who source and negotiate discreetly off-market, and prestige real estate agencies that offer buyer-side services or access to high-end property networks.** They can all be valuable, but they don't offer the same level of independence or depth of acquisition advice.

For a multimillion-dollar home, the best adviser should do more than find attractive listings. They should identify opportunities before they reach the market, assess fair value, investigate comparable sales and property risks, negotiate strategically, and coordinate due diligence through to settlement.

## My shortlist of Australian prestige property advisers

The following are the firms I would investigate first, depending on the city, type of property and level of acquisition support required. This is a qualitative shortlist, not a verified ranking of transaction success or client satisfaction.

items.markdown:
These are best-fit matches based on their published services and market focus, not proof that one firm consistently achieves better purchase prices than another.

## Prestige real estate agencies versus independent buyers' advocates

If you are purchasing a home worth, say, \$5 million to \$20 million or more, I would consider the following distinction particularly important.

**Independent buyers' advocates**

They are engaged to represent your interests, source properties, advise on value and negotiate. This is generally my preferred model for a buyer who wants confidential, unconflicted acquisition advice. The Real Estate Buyers Agents Association of Australia (REBAA) outlines independence, licensing and conflict-of-interest standards for its members. [rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/buyers-agents/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/REBAA-Code-of-Conduct-2024-Edition-v5.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

**Prestige sales agencies**

Firms such as Ray White and Kollosche can be useful sources of market intelligence, listing access and introductions to premium properties. Kollosche is especially relevant to the Gold Coast prestige market. [www.couriermail.com.au](https://www.couriermail.com.au/property/gold-coast-luxury-property-market-defies-national-downturn-as-wealthy-interstate-buyers-invest/news-story/7e04ade24dcc8907cb6a9ff61953cbfb?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.couriermail.com.au](https://www.couriermail.com.au/real-estate/queensland/gold-coast/economist-reveals-major-shift-in-gold-coast-property-market/news-story/4995cd6b00c7465cf45b7259ccc6850d?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

However, a selling agent's primary responsibility is to the vendor. I would use these agencies as sources of opportunities rather than assume their advice is equivalent to independent buyer representation.

## What to demand from an acquisition adviser

For a prestige purchase, I would insist on six things before signing an engagement agreement\:

1. **Relevant transactions\:** Three recent purchases comparable in price, suburb and property type, with client references where possible.
2. **Genuine off-market access\:** Evidence of relevant opportunities sourced before public listing, not just a large contact database.
3. **Independent valuation discipline\:** Comparable sales, a defensible price range, an assessment of the property's weaknesses and a clear walk-away price.
4. **Confidentiality\:** A documented process for protecting your identity, budget and negotiating position.
5. **Full due diligence\:** Coordination with your conveyancer or solicitor, building and pest inspectors, and relevant planning or specialist advisers.
6. **Transparent fees and conflicts\:** Written disclosure of commissions, referral payments, developer relationships and any other financial interests.

REBAA publishes useful guidance on choosing an advocate and typical fee structures. Its published industry guidance puts full-service fees commonly around 2–3% of the purchase price plus GST, although fixed-fee arrangements and more limited negotiation-only services are also available. Obtain individual quotes rather than treating this as a universal tariff. [rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/buyers-agents/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/faqs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The best shortlist will change significantly depending on where you want to buy and whether you need discreet access to exceptional homes or a broader property-acquisition strategy.

Melbourne — Toorak, Brighton, South Yarra and inner east
